hook: SCP-699 is a transparent, seamless box weighing around 24 tonnes that shows each viewer something different inside. It turned up without warning and promptly crashed down through several floors of a Foundation site. Look closely at what is engraved on the case and at the damaged document that came with it.
whyItMatters:
Its core idea is perception as a trap. Most people see something they want and feel an urge to open the case, a small minority see something terrifying, and that frightened minority is exactly who the procedures put on guard.

It also plays with the notion of a containment file arriving from the Foundation's own future, and because most of that file is unreadable, much of the work is left to the reader.
thingsToNotice:
The engraving gives the box a Keter symbol and a different item number, and the damaged report backs it up: a Foundation record running from 2455 to 2466 about an entity bent on carrying out something called Protocol Z, able to influence people from a distance, that escaped at least once and pushed staff into terminating two of their own colleagues. The last entry orders an experimental procedure 'T' and mentions the people of a receiving timeline, which is where the box landed.

That puts the 9 percent who see danger, and the two doctors who see nothing at all, in a new light, although the article never confirms whose view is accurate. The closing notes add a dry edge, with a records clerk refusing to file it under its future number and an O5 telling staff not to dump troublesome objects into the nearest portal.
